text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The Japanese Red Army says in a statement in Japan that some of its members were arrested in Lebanon.
-Hizbollah chief Sheikh Nasrallah: "We are getting closer to the time when Israel leaves south Lebanon".
-Intra Investment Company increases its capital to 280 billion Lebanese pounds from 280 million pounds.
-Foreign Minister Bouez discusses with papal nuncio Puente the Pope's visit to Lebanon in May.
-Japan's ambassador in Beirut handed Foreign Minister Bouez a letter demanding information about a number of detainees reported held in Beirut and suspected of belonging to the Japanese Red Army.
-Fransabank says in its Q4 report that the Lebanese economy grew by four percent in 1996 compared with 6.5 percent a year earlier.
-Beirut Stock Exchange chairman Sehnaoui says that the bourse committee will finish studying within two weeks the file of Byblos Bank, which wants to trade 30 percent of its shares on the market.
